purpose: Worked example of a trigger-eval set. These 20 queries were used to test make-skill-and-publish itself on 2026-10-10; copy the shape, not the content, when testing a different skill.
how_it_was_run: Routing: one fresh agent saw only the skill descriptions (this skill plus skill-creator, skill-installer, documents as distractors) and judged each query, without being told the expected labels.
Behaviour: two further fresh agents were given a should-trigger query and a near-miss query as real tasks and reported whether any skill was actually loaded.

outcome.fix_applied: Removed 'install a skill from a repo' from the description: it overlapped skill-installer and pulled in Q11. Also narrowed 'publish it to GitHub' to 'publish that skill to GitHub' and dropped the over-broad fallback clause.

known_gaps: Q14 (review an existing SKILL.md) is genuinely uncovered: neither this skill nor skill-creator claims 'review / audit an existing skill' in its description. Left as a known gap rather than expanding this skill's scope on low-confidence evidence.
'workflow' is still a slightly risky word in the description, because GitHub Actions workflows share it.
